conventions.convention: Criticality means failure of local real analyticity of the finite pointwise limiting pressure p(θ)=lim N_n⁻¹ log Z_n(θ), on a nonempty open parameter interval. This is only the nonanalytic-pressure criterion.

The dimensionless precision K appears in exp(−zᵀKz/2), with Euclidean Lebesgue reference measure and covariance K⁻¹. Countable Choice is assumed. In dimension zero the space is a singleton, its probability has mass one, and its partition factor and determinant equal one.

The periodic Laplacian is (−Δf)(x)=Σ_j(2f(x)−f(x+e_j)−f(x−e_j)); both shift terms are counted even when they coincide at L=1 or L=2. Characters use positive exponential sign and inner product L⁻ᵈΣ_x f(x) conjugate(g(x)).
The periodic lattice precision is m²I+κ(−Δ), with m²>0 and κ>0 in dimensionless lattice units. The unrestricted zero-mass torus weight is not a probability density.

The Green integral uses D_d(k)=4Σ_j sin²(k_j/2), the cube [−π,π]ᵈ, normalization (2π)⁻ᵈ and numerator cos(k·x). The integrand is assigned zero at the null singleton k=0. The threshold concerns this Fourier integral only.

Retained coordinate sets are nested and increasingly ordered. Each nonempty eliminated block contributes Schur complement A−BC⁻¹Bᵀ and log factor |E| log(2π)/2−log(det C)/2; an empty elimination contributes zero. The procedure uses exact arithmetic.
Engineering scaling uses b>0 and φ_b(x)=b^{−(d−2)/2}φ′(x/b) on real smooth compactly supported test fields; the quartic functional includes the factor 1/4!.

load_bearing.statement: Under Countable Choice, a real symmetric positive-definite K defines the centered probability with density Z_K⁻¹ exp(−zᵀKz/2), normalizer Z_K=(2π)^{N/2}(det K)^{−1/2}, and covariance K⁻¹; the zero-dimensional probability and partition factor are defined separately.

For a symmetric positive-definite block matrix K=[[A,B],[Bᵀ,C]] with retained size r≥0 and eliminated size s≥1, C is positive definite with positive determinant and inverse; S=A−BC⁻¹Bᵀ is positive definite for r≥1 and empty for r=0. The stated completion-of-the-square identity holds for every x and y.

For integers d,L≥1, the periodic characters form an orthonormal basis and have Laplacian eigenvalues 4Σ_j sin²(πr_j/L). Consequently −Δ is real symmetric positive semidefinite, and m²I+κ(−Δ) is positive definite for m²>0 and κ>0.

Under Countable Choice and the algorithm hypotheses, the procedure terminates after q stages, preserves positive definiteness on nonempty retained spaces, and integrates the eliminated coordinates exactly to exp(Σ_j ℓ_j) exp(−xᵀK_qx/2). The retained marginal is the stated Gaussian, including the singleton convention, and log Z_K₀=Σ_j ℓ_j+log Z_Kq.
For |u|≤π/2, 2|u|/π≤|sin u|≤|u|. For all real u,v, |sin u−sin v|≤|u−v|.
Under Countable Choice, for integers d,L≥1 and κ>0, the unrestricted Euclidean Lebesgue integral of exp(−zᵀκ(−Δ)z/2) on the periodic lattice coordinate space is +∞.
